newsitem.title: GERMANY: Flood-hit Poland, Germany mount mass evacuations.
newsitem.headline: Flood-hit Poland, Germany mount mass evacuations.

text.p: More than 15,000 people were evacuated on Sunday from the town of Slubice on the Oder (Odra) river between Poland and Germany as it rose to record high levels and threatened to swamp the area.
On the other side of the Oder, 19,000 Germans in the Oderbruch plains braced for mass evacuations after a third flood barrier reinforcing the banks of the surging river burst further upstream.

The evacuation in Slubice, across the river from the German city of Frankfurt an der Oder, came as Polish Interior Minister Leszek Miller met his German counterpart Manfred Kanther there to discuss coordinating efforts to combat the disaster.

Polish flood committee spokeswoman Lidia Markindorf said Slubice, situated in a low-lying area, could be hit by a huge flood surge any time if the eroded and sodden protection dikes along the Oder burst despite frantic sand-bagging.
"The situation in Slubice is dangerous. We have seen the Odra's level increasing by 40 cm...and dikes are soaked," private Radio Zet quoted Markindorf as saying.
Radio Zet reported that those who refused to be evacuated from Slubice had to sign special statements declaring they were staying at their own risk.
In Germany, around 5,000 residents were evacuated from the Oderbruch plains on Friday and officials there advised the rest to be prepared to leave their homes at any time.
A large section of the dike in Oderbruch and two other dikes south of Frankfurt an der Oder further upstream have collapsed over the past few days.
Emergency teams of up to 12,000 soldiers, border guards and volunteers worked round the clock to shore them up in Germany's biggest peacetime operation since World War Two.

"We are preparing the entire Oderbruch region for a possible evacuation," said Ralph Leidenheimer, a spokesman for the Brandenburg interior ministry. "There is the acute danger that it could come to a break in the dike."

The Oderbruch plain , 50 km (30 miles) long and 17 km (11 miles) wide, was reclaimed 250 years ago by Prussian King Frederick the Great who drained the moors there to create a large fertile basin for farmland.
It lies lower than the river itself and any serious break in the 70-km (45 mile)-long flood barriers would mean the entire region including 17 villages and farmland would be submerged.

German officials monitoring the floods said water levels north of Brieskow-Finkenheerd, which is near a dike that burst overnight creating a one-km (mile) wide gap, were rising as flood water trapped inland flowed back into the river.
Flooding over the last three weeks, the worst natural disaster in the region for centuries, has claimed over 100 lives in Poland and the Czech Republic and caused billions of dollars in damage.
